newsitem.title: UK: Queens Moat sees encouraging outlook.
newsitem.headline: Queens Moat sees encouraging outlook.

text.p: Debt-laden hotel group Queens Moat Houses Plc said on Thursday it regarded prospects for future growth as "encouraging" after a return to full-year pre-tax profit in 1996.
"Overall, the board regards the prospects for future growth as encouraging," chairman Stanley Metcalfe said.
"After two months trading in the current year, I can report that the group has made further progress," he added.
Queens Moat said net borrowings were down from 1.016 billion to 842 million stg following the sale of 25 UK hotels earlier this month.
Queens Moat sold 25 hotels to a management buy-in for 91.5 million stg, leaving it a core UK portfolio of 49 properties.

Metcalfe said the UK division was achieving strong occupancies and growth in room rates but added the group was wary of the effects of strong sterling and possible higher interest rates after the May 1 election.
Operating profits from continuing business in the UK rose by almost 12 percent to 33.5 million stg in 1996.
Metcalfe noted economic improvement in Germany was slow but that the company was well placed to take advantage of improvements there in the medium term.

Its Dutch Bilderberg chain was reported responding positively to more focused management and higher capital expenditure while France and Belgium were benefiting from actions to improve under-performing hotels.
Operating profits from Germany were 4.7 million stg in 1996 against 1.1 million the year before. The Dutch division reported earnings of 12.1 million stg, up from 10.2 million.
Queens Moat broke even in France and had a loss of 300,000 stg in Belgium.
